passages.provision_quote: In response to the congressional redistricting in Texas in 2025, and notwithstanding any other provision of this Constitution or existing law, the single-member districts for Congress reflected in Assembly Bill 604 of the 2025–26 Regular Session pursuant to the requirements of Chapter 5 (commencing with Section 21400) of Division 21 of the Elections Code shall temporarily be used for every congressional election for a term of office commencing on or after the date this subdivision becomes operative and before the certification of new congressional boundary lines drawn by the Citizens Redistricting Commission pursuant to subdivision (d).
passages.note: The measure's two operative parts point opposite ways on who draws the maps: it declares state policy for independent nonpartisan commissions and restores the Citizens Redistricting Commission in 2031, while temporarily substituting legislature-drawn congressional maps.

rows.reasoning: ACA 8 (2025-2026), authored by Rivas, declares it "the policy of the State of California to support the use of fair, independent, and nonpartisan redistricting commissions nationwide" and keeps the Citizens Redistricting Commission drawing the lines in 2031, while temporarily substituting legislature-drawn congressional maps from AB 604 until then. That does not match "independent citizens' commissions with no elected officials involved at any level" — the measure never says no elected officials, and it has elected officials draw the interim maps — nor "the party that controls the state legislature without outside interference", since the override is temporary, requires the people's approval, and leaves the Attorney General and the California Supreme Court as checks. A single instrument whose operative sections cut both ways shows a side at most, not one rung.
